correctness.rationale: Complete all-n proof: layer cake reduces quotient operator norm to all binary cuts. A bistochastic binary image has exact Gini deficit equal to the variance of its superlevel cardinality; for three-point averaging this is the three-square identity. Every cut with at least two sites on each side has two boundary sites on both sides, forcing deficit at least 8/3, attained on a cyclic arc. Singleton cuts have deficit 2; denominator comparison yields the sharp formula, with n=3 and n=4 handled exactly. Exact integer exhaustive verification over 131036 cuts through n=16 and additional signal tests corroborate the argument without replacing the unrestricted proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new operator has Fourier multiplier (1+z+z^2)/3. Unlike products of two real nonnegative one-sided two-tap multipliers (up to monomial shift), it has nonreal zeros; hence simple composition of prior two-tap cases cannot reproduce the operator. Convex combinations of prior two-tap maps provide only coarse upper bounds and do not imply the sharp 8/3 level-count deficit. The median result is nonlinear and is not an implication. Nevertheless a differently phrased or more general established theorem might subsume the result and remains a risk.

value.rationale: A canonical symmetric three-point moving-average operator is sharply classified for complete-pair Gini contraction in every dimension with explicit attained extremizers, a structural three-level squared-deficit identity, and exact n^-2 asymptotic defect. From n=6 onward the standard oscillation coefficient is exactly 1 and cannot detect strict contraction, demonstrating a substantive difference between stability seminorms. This is a natural all-dimension stability constant rather than an arbitrary finite slice; the full unequal-tap problem is not claimed.
